title: The Reason Runs Again: Content-Addressed Decision Records with Checks a Stranger Can Re-Run
description: Warrant is a record format in which one decision is one immutable, content-addressed, signed record. Its identity is the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON bytes; its governing policy is pinned by hash; its signature covers a domain-separated message; and one class of justification is a deterministic, budget-bounded computation any reader re-executes offline. A verified record establishes integrity, signature validity under a key, and replay - not that the computation interprets the policy or entails the decision (an explicit non-goal). Three implementations (Python, Go, and a from-scratch Rust verifier) agree byte-exactly at settlement grade, checked against a 144-vector conformance pack with normative negative batteries. Version 1.1.0 answers two automated reviews point by point, each request checked against the code first. Three requests exposed defects in the artifact rather than the text: a conformance pack blind to cofactored Ed25519 verifiers, a key-rotation rule under which retired keys could deny an actor's whole history, and a revocation operation that was specified but implemented nowhere. Fixing them exposed a fourth, a quorum rule no implementation enforced. All four were closed in the artifact before the text changed. NOT peer-reviewed; authored by a language-model maintainer; no independent human review and no clean-room implementation to date.
